headline: Estone Technology acquires One SeaGate, announces HQ move and tech hub vision — Toledo's 32-story downtown tower gets its new-owner repositioning plan
paragraphs: One SeaGate — the 32-story, 653,421-square-foot office tower along the Maumee River that defines Toledo's downtown skyline — has been sold to local investors, Reichle Klein Group (RKG) announced August 27–28, 2026. The buyers were not identified by name at the time; RKG confirmed they are local investors. Ryan Miller, senior vice president at RKG, represented the buyer in the transaction. Harlan Reichle, president and CEO of RKG, and Chad Ulmer, a sales associate, represented the seller. No sale price was disclosed. This marks the second time RKG has sold the building.

Completed in the early 1980s, One SeaGate served as the global headquarters of Owens-Illinois until the glass and packaging company relocated in 2006. The tower — Toledo's tallest commercial building — occupies a prominent riverfront address at 1 Seagate in the central business district and has been the city's most recognizable office asset for more than four decades.

Estone Technology, a Holland-area industrial technology company specializing in panel PCs and rugged computing solutions, announced September 3, 2026 that its owner and a business partner acquired One SeaGate and that the company plans to relocate its corporate headquarters into the building. The announcement identifies the 'local investors' behind the August 27 transaction. Estone intends to bring smart-building technologies to the property in phases — planned upgrades include modern smart security and access-control systems, connected building-management technologies, improved digital communications, and robotic cleaning solutions. The company described a long-term vision for One SeaGate as a 'regional center for technology and innovation, serving businesses across Ohio, Michigan, and the broader Midwest.'

The headquarters relocation, technology enhancements, parking improvements, and new amenities will roll out in phases, the company said. Estone stated it plans to continue investing in its Toledo-area operations and creating opportunities for future business growth and hiring. No financial details of the acquisition, specific lease terms, or a timeline for the phased improvements have been disclosed.

Property records filed September 10, 2026 and reported by The Blade and WTOL on September 10–11 confirmed the full transaction structure: One SeaGate sold through two separate deals totaling $9.5 million. One Seagate Holdings LLC paid $8.9 million to One Seagate Partners LLC for the building, structures, and improvements; a second transaction transferred the underlying land from Seagate Land Partners LLC to One Seagate Holdings for $600,000. The deeds took effect August 27 and were recorded by Lucas County on September 10. The acquisition was financed with a $5 million commercial mortgage and $4.5 million in cash. The $9.5 million figure — for Toledo's tallest commercial tower at 653,421 square feet — reflects the regional office market conditions the central business district has navigated since Owens-Illinois departed in 2006; it also positions Estone's acquisition cost low enough that a phased repositioning and innovation-hub investment strategy is financially viable even with a large share of the building still to lease.
why_it_matters: This is the repositioning announcement Toledo's downtown development stakeholders have been waiting for since the August 27 sale. Estone Technology's decision to anchor a technology company's headquarters at One SeaGate — and to frame the 32-story tower as a regional innovation hub — is a materially different signal than a stabilization or passive-hold strategy. If Estone's phased smart-building upgrades and tenant-attraction vision advances, it could seed the kind of tech-adjacent office demand that Toledo's central business district has not had since Owens-Illinois departed in 2006. The critical questions are execution and tenant recruitment: a single company's headquarters occupying a portion of a 653,000-square-foot tower does not fill it, and the 'innovation hub' vision only validates if other companies follow. Watch for any tenant announcements, the pace of visible building upgrades, and whether Estone's owner begins publicly recruiting co-tenants.
